text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Peru sets stage for hostage talks: Men held in Japanese embassy calm but sleeping on floor, Canadian mediator says.
- Exodus of Quebec residents biggest since summer of '83.
- Doctor quit over blood safety: Replacing physicians with lay people worried former head of Red Cross program.
- Longer school is N.B. aim: In at 5, out at 18, would be rule.
- Protests growing against Milosevic: Braving threats 250,000 turn out.
- Markets roar back to life: Toronto, New York post big gains on bond rally, good news about U.S. economy.
- Newbridge adds U.S. sales force to stable: Buys unit from Tandem Computer for up to $100 million.
- Bay Street giant Austin Taylor dead: Built ScotiaMcLeod into a powerhouse.
- Bank seeks a T-bill crackdown: Central bank calls for trading rules to avoid manipulation.
- Bay Street giant Austin Taylor dead: Built ScotiaMcLeod into a powerhouse.
- Markets roar back: Stocks and bonds shake free of the woes that beset them earlier this month but the reasons differ. Bonds react to signals of a slowdown. Stocks seize on news of economic growth.
- Newbridge snaps up UB Networks for 'nice price' of US$150 million.
